podcast.title: "At the Quinte Hotel" Poem
podcast.body: For those looking to explore Purdy's work, the poem "At the Quinte Hotel," set in Belleville, Ontario, is recommended. It's a satirical piece that discusses beer, the relationship between art and commerce, and humorously depicts a bar fight where the author eventually wins over the crowd with his verses. "look up a poem called at the Quente Hotel, which is set in Belleville, Ontario."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on Gord Downie
podcast.body: Gord Downie frequently returned to Purdy's work, appearing in a short film based on "At the Quinte Hotel" (2002), reciting the poem during a MuchMusic performance, and featuring in a 2015 documentary about Purdy. Downie also contributed to the documentary's soundtrack, which included songs and poems inspired by Purdy. "Gord Danny would return to Albert E. Time and Time again."

podcast.title: Unofficial Poet Laureate of Canada
podcast.body: Al Purdy had a career spanning 56 years, publishing 39 books of poetry, two memoirs, a novel, and four collections of letters. He was widely regarded as Canada's unofficial poet laureate and a master storyteller. "Perdi was considered to be Canada's unofficial poet laureate, a great teller of myths and stories."

xref.title: Collaboration with Al Purdy
xref.body: Downie frequently returned to the work of Canadian poet Al Purdy. In 2002, he appeared in a five-minute short film based on Purdy's poem "At the Quinte Hotel," with Purdy himself also providing a voice. Downie also performed a recitation of the poem during a MuchMusic performance and appeared in a 2015 documentary on Purdy, which included a soundtrack featuring songs and poems inspired by Purdy, to which Downie contributed "The East Wind." "In 2002, Gord appeared in a five minute short film based on the poem."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Contribution to Al Purdy Tribute
xref.body: Bruce Cobra and Greg Keelor from Blue Rodeo were among the artists who contributed to the soundtrack of the 2015 documentary on Al Purdy, which featured songs and poems inspired by the poet. "Bruce Cobra and Greg Kieler of Blue Rodeo, Sarah Harmer, Jason Collette of Broken Social Scene, even Margaret Atwood appeared on that album."

xref.title: Poetic Influences and Reading List
xref.body: Gord Downie deeply engaged with poetry, reading works by Leonard Cohen, Al Purdy, and Irvin Layton. His novel reading list included books by Margaret Atwood and he also read Northrop Frye, a highly influential 20th-century Canadian literary critic. "He also really got into reading poetry. Leonard Cohen, L. Perty, Irvin Layton."
